This paper conducts a sentiment analysis across languages, examining the
emotional content of news articles using both few-shot and zero-shot learning
techniques. The primary objective is to categorize Croatian news articles as
expressing positive, negative, or neutral sentiment, employing a dataset from
Slovene. The underlying model is a multilingual BERT-based system, pre-trained
on three languages: English, Slovene, and Croatian. The paper investigates
various setups utilizing datasets from two languages and presents a straightforward
multi-task model to accomplish sentiment classification. The assessment involves
zero-shot and few-shot learning approaches within single-task and multi-task
experiments for both Slovene and Croatian.

X-ray images contain subtle characteristics that may indicate certain clinical conditions. If these features can be easily extracted and used as inputs for machine learning models, they could help predict severe symptoms associated with COVID-19. If not all extractable features are obvious, automatically learning methods, such as convolutional neural networks, can help identify them. If such networks trained on normal and abnormal X-rays can only slightly differentiate between severe and mild symptoms, it suggests that already extractable features may something other than that severity. To investigate this, we used state-of-the-art models trained on X-ray data sets and tested them on COVID-19 patients, then analyzed their activations to predict symptom severity. We found that most features extracted did not correlate with severity, and that current state-of-the-art models may not have captured features related to symptom severity. Our findings highlight the need to extract features that are directly related to severity and highlight limitations of using conventional evaluation methods. Ultimately, we believe that conventional evaluation methods may mask important aspects that are not directly related to the primary objective.

The classical universal bundle functor W mapping from the category of simplicial groups in C to the category of simplicial sets in C lifts to a functor that operates on the category of simplicial algebras in C to the category of simplicial algebras in E(C). This result holds for any variety of algebraic structures defined by identities of finite length.

This paper delves into the source of high false positive rates in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD). During training, we discovered that the relationship proposal distribution is skewed, with the majority of incorrect proposals being low-confidence, bipartite graph edges that connect two objects without a connection between them. A bidirectional proposal graph, which accounts for these implicit edges, is proposed to correct this distortion and improve model performance. To address the class imbalance of edges, Sample Balance Learning (SBL) is also introduced. In experiments, significant improvements in the Mean Proposal Accuracy and COCO test-set results are achieved by integrating the bidirectional proposal graph and SBL. Code is available at https://github.com/PranavJain17/SAVED.

We've performed an in-depth analysis of three galaxy cores at $\rm z=2.94$ within a massive galaxy group, utilizing deep imaging and spectroscopic data.
These galaxies exhibit significant characteristics of low star-formation efficiency despite active disk growth, and are dominated by bulge features.
We've identified two star-forming clumps in each galaxy, and calculated their masses, formation rates, and ages.
These rates, when compared to Hubble predictions, appear modest for galaxies of this mass, and may be attributed to limited gas available for star formation due to lopsided disk structures.
We've also categorized the remaining gas in these galaxies as being located in quasi-halo layers, and suggest that maintenance of disk-umbrella structures is contributing to the observed low star-formation rates by deflecting cold gas away from the disk and into hotter, less efficient layers.
This phenomenon, in conjunction with suppressed star formation in galaxy cores with lopsided disks, may be key components of a novel theoretical framework for evolution based on thermal rather than mechanical properties, and could potentially be explored through a corresponding "hot major merger" stage in the cosmological $\Lambda$CDM model.

Recently discovered solar observations from Bolivia (5250 m above sea level) and Mexico (4600 m above sea level) uncovered a significant event on November 7, 2004, linked to a powerful X2.0 solar flare. Analysis of recorded data, along with satellite observations from GOES 11 and SOHO, suggest that neutrons may have broken down into electrons and protons. Historically, evidence of this process was found on board ISEE3 on June 3rd, 1982 and through ground detectors in Goose Bay and Deep River on October 19th, 1989, providing a second terrestrial instance of this occurrence.

This study reveals intriguing evidence of a complex internal rotation pattern within a less massive and less luminous star that has evolved into a giant. Typically, lower and intermediate mass stars retain their rapid rotation rates during their main sequence phase. However, once these stars expand into giants, we expect a faster core rotation rate compared to their outer layers. Contrary to these expectations, KIC 9267654's rotation speed is observed to be higher near its surface rather than at its core, which presents a challenge to angular momentum conservation principles. To validate our findings, we updated the constraints based on spectroscopic surface measurements, verified that the detected oscillation patterns align with the previously determined core and outer layer rotation rates, and confirmed that the star does not exhibit any significant chemical composition differences that could influence our interpretation. To explain the observed core and outer layer rotation rates, we explored various theories related to angular momentum preservation, including the role of angular momentum transfer, internal gravity waves, and differential rotation. Unfortunately, none of these mechanisms can effectively explain the observed rotation rates without making unrealistic assumptions. As a star like KIC 9267654, with a core and outer layer rotating in the opposite direction, offers a rare and valuable opportunity to study the preservation of angular momentum in a less massive and less luminous giant star, we propose that further in-depth observations and modeling are necessary to explain the star's rotation pattern.

Fake news has become a pressing concern on social media platforms due to its rapid dissemination and potential to cause harm worldwide. Although machine learning models have been successful in detecting false information, especially when large amounts of labeled data are available, their effectiveness significantly declines when they are applied to emerging events. This limitation stems from the fact that many pieces of fake news are not semantically similar to each other, making it extremely challenging for current models to identify false information on emerging events, especially when they are forced to operate in open-set scenarios. To address this challenge, we propose a novel framework called F3N, which aims to detect false information on emerging events, even when they are not contained within an predefined set. The F3N framework consists of three main components: a semantic-aware fake news encoder to capture both common and unique characteristics, including those that are emerging; a dynamic prototyping module to manage the balance between shared and unique features; and a tri-class detector that is designed to handle multiple classes of false information. Experiments conducted on large-scale Twitter datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the F3N framework in identifying false information on emerging events, outperforming state-of-the-art methods and achieving significant improvements of 5.3% and 9.3% over current techniques in closed- and open-set settings, respectively.

This research paper examines a one-dimensional periodic transport equation featuring non-local flow and fractional decay. The equation in question is given by $$
u_{t}-(Hu)_{x}u_{x}+\kappa\Lambda^{\alpha}u=0,\quad (t,x)\in R^{+}\times S.
$$
Where $S$ denotes the domain, we have $\kappa\geq0$, $0<\alpha\leq1$, and investigate the well-posedness of this transport equation within $H^{3}(S)$ for a limited time frame. It is demonstrated that when $\kappa$ equals zero and the initial data is smooth and odd, the solution will blow up in a finite time unless $\|u_{0x}\|_{L^{\infty}}$ is also less than the norm $\|u_{0}\|_{L^{\infty}}$. However, when $\kappa$ is greater than zero, we find that the corresponding solution remains global when the initial data is smooth. Additionally, we also establish the stability of the solution when $\alpha$ is between one and equal to two.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained popularity due to their utility in omnidirectional precoding techniques. This research extends Golay complementary matrices to higher-dimensional spaces known as multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays and presents novel construction methods for pairs and quadruples of GCA. A set of ring identities is introduced to facilitate these constructions. Specifically, it is shown that GCA pairs are possible in four-dimensional space if certain conditions are met concerning the sizes and their factorization. Additionally, in binary GCM quadruples, possible sizes are postulated as unlimited, which is confirmed for sizes 78x78 and a few scattered instances, whereas all positive integers below 1000 can be covered in a one-dimensional space of a quaternary GCM quad.

Quantum tunneling and interactions between silicon dopants are critical in designing and understanding devices like qubits and diodes.  However, because the mass of silicon's quantum-tipped particles is quite high, direct computation of their distribution is challenging due to the related multi-body uncertainty.  In this study, we present an efficient method to address this issue by combining two formulas to describe point mass behavior in one and three dimensions with impurity density in two and three-dimensional systems.  By inverting the density function using a relationship with mass in one dimension, we derived an explicit density formula for point masses in one dimension.  In addition, we developed an algorithm to find density in three dimensions using Monte Carlo simulation.  In this paper, we demonstrate the application of the introduced method to point mass distribution in a one-dimensional system and a three-dimensional system with a Monte Carlo model.  In doing so, we successfully computed the wave function and coordinate of a double-barrier system through the introduced density relation, demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in dealing with real-world problems.

Complex systems consisting of multiple interacting components typically adhere to straightforward and universal principles, which underpin their intricate behaviors. Despite graph neural networks offering valuable insights for modeling these complex interactions, there's still a significant gap in understanding how to effectively generalize to novel instances of the system within the framework of scientific machine learning. In this research, we introduce a novel graph neural network model that captures essential interactions by developing a network of linearly connected components, which apply local laws to produce a representation of the entire system. This model is shown to accurately predict diverse phenomena including heat diffusion, fluid dynamics, and pattern recognition. Furthermore, it can learn to model the dynamics of previously unseen instances of the same system type, as well as more intricate system types with altered interactions or network structures.

We introduce an infinite family of recursive formulas for calculating the counts of binary integer partitions that fulfill specific divisibility criteria, establishing relationships between $b(n,k)$ and both $b(n,j)$ where $j$ is less than $n$, as well as $b(2n,k)$ and $b(n,k)$. These formulas can be depicted as lower triangular matrices with diagonal entries equal to $2$, exhibiting a structure that displays a form of sparsest positivity, and thus possess the property of being the inverse of an LDLC matrix. This characteristic enables the establishment of the following identity which holds particularly for the count of all binary partitions of an integer $n$.

A cutting-edge, minimally invasive therapy called Laser Interstitial Thermal Therapy (LITT) treats seizures caused by epilepsy in a specific brain area, the mesial temporal lobe. Evaluating the effectiveness of this treatment requires analyzing changes to the treated brain area after LITT, which can be achieved through advanced brain imaging techniques such as Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI). In a new study, DTI analysis methods based on tensor orientation are shown to be equally effective as traditional mean fractional anisotropy (FA) and fractional anisotropy volume (FAV) measures in identifying alterations to the treated brain tissue. Machine learning techniques were also incorporated, which, although adding processing complexity, resulted in only marginally better outcomes. Ultimately, the study finds that a simple, two-layer neural model outperforms more complex alternatives, which has significant implications for clinical settings where processing time and resources are limited.
